name: Maine
gaps: The municipal excise tax is based on the maker's list price (MSRP) of the model, not the price paid; when the MSRP is not typed, the engine uses the price, which understates the excise of a discounted new car and of any used car.
Inspection amounts are the legal maximum fees of 29-A M.R.S. §1751 ($12.50, or $18.50 for the enhanced inspection required in Cumberland County); a station may charge less.
Municipalities can add a small agent fee when the town office processes the registration; it varies by town and is not added.
No dealer documentation fee cap exists in Maine law (a 2023 bill to limit the fee, LD 639, died); type the dealer's fee. It is taxed at 5.5% as part of the sale price.
On a private sale the 5.5% use tax is computed on the price declared; the engine does not check it against a book value.

summary.docFeeNote: No cap in Maine law (LD 639 of 2023 died); the fee is part of the taxable sale price.
summary.inspectionWhere: Yearly safety inspection for every registered car; in Cumberland County it is an enhanced inspection that adds the OBD emissions check for 1996 and newer models.

tax.label: Sales and use tax (5.5%)
tax.note: 5.5% of the price minus the trade-in allowance; dealer documentation fees are part of the taxable price.

once.label: Certificate of title
once.note: The $33 includes the first security interest (lien).

valueFees.label: Municipal excise tax (mills on the MSRP by model year)
valueFees.note: 24 mills per dollar of the MSRP in the first year of the model, then 17.5, 13.5, 10, 6.5 and 4 mills from the sixth year; paid to your town before registering.

inspection.label: Yearly safety inspection (legal maximum)
inspection.note: Maximum fee a station may charge; a car bought from a dealer comes with a current sticker.

inspection.label: Yearly enhanced inspection with OBD check, Cumberland County (legal maximum)
inspection.note: Maximum fee for a 1996 or newer car; a car bought from a dealer comes with a current sticker.

singular: Maine's yearly car tax is a municipal excise paid to your town before the state registers the car, set by statute at 24 mills per dollar of the maker's list price in the model's first year [excise].
The excise rate falls with the model year: 17.5 mills in the second year, 13.5 in the third, 10 in the fourth, 6.5 in the fifth and 4 mills from the sixth year on, with a $5 minimum [excise].
Because the excise follows the list price and not the price paid, a dealer discount does not lower it; buyers of a new car hand the MSRP sticker to the excise collector [excise].
The state sales and use tax is 5.5% of the price, the same general rate as other goods [rate].
When a car is traded toward another car, the 5.5% applies only to the difference between the price and the trade-in allowance [trade-in].
A private sale of a car is not exempt: Maine levies its tax on casual sales of motor vehicles [casual].
Maine Revenue Services treats dealer processing and documentation fees as part of the taxable sale price [ib24].
A one-year automobile registration costs $35, and a certificate of title costs $33 [reg].
Every registered car needs a yearly inspection; stations may charge at most $12.50, or $18.50 for the enhanced inspection required in Cumberland County [inspection].
Maine has no electric or hybrid registration surcharge in its registration fee statute; an automobile pays the same $35 whatever its fuel [reg].

excise.name: 36 M.R.S. §1482, Excise tax
excise.quote: a sum equal to 24 mills on each dollar of the maker's list price for the first or current year of model, 17 1/2 mills for the 2nd year, 13 1/2 mills for the 3rd year, 10 mills for the 4th year, 6 1/2 mills for the 5th year and 4 mills for the 6th and succeeding years. The minimum tax is $5

rate.name: 36 M.R.S. §1811, Sales tax rate
rate.quote: For sales occurring on or after October 1, 2019, the rate of tax is 5.5% on the value of all tangible personal property and taxable services

trade-in.name: 36 M.R.S. §1765, Trade-in credit
trade-in.quote: the tax imposed by this Part must be levied only upon the difference between the sale price of the purchased property and the trade-in allowance of the property taken in trade ... 1. Motor vehicles.

casual.name: 36 M.R.S. §1764, Tax against certain casual sales
casual.quote: The tax imposed by this Part must be levied ... upon all casual sales ... involving the sale of trailers, truck campers, motor vehicles

ib24.name: Maine Revenue Services, Instructional Bulletin No. 24, Vehicle Dealers (12/22/2025)
ib24.quote: All charges imposed by a dealer for services that are part of the sale are considered part of the sale price of the vehicle and are subject to sales tax. Examples include: “Processing fees” or “documentation fees.”

title.name: 29-A M.R.S. §603, Fees (certificate of title)
title.quote: A fee of $33 must be paid to the Secretary of State for the following: ... B. Filing an application for a first certificate of title, including security interest; ... D. A certificate of title after a transfer

reg.name: 29-A M.R.S. §501, Fees for registration; motor vehicles
reg.quote: The fee for an automobile, a pickup truck registered for 6,000 pounds or less or a sport utility vehicle used for the conveyance of passengers or interchangeably for passengers or property is $35.

inspection.name: 29-A M.R.S. §1751, Motor vehicle inspection
inspection.quote: a motor vehicle required to be registered in this State must have an annual inspection ... For inspections performed under subsection 2, the fee may not be more than $12.50 ... 1996 and subsequent model vehicles performed under subsection 2-A, the fee may not be more than $18.50.

dealer-insp.name: 29-A M.R.S. §1754, Inspection by dealers and transporters
dealer-insp.quote: Is sold or transferred to another person, meets inspection standards and displays a valid certificate of inspection issued within 60 days of the sale or transfer

doc-fee.name: Maine Legislature, LD 639 (131st), An Act to Protect Vehicle Buyers by Limiting Vehicle Document Preparation Fees
